items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I mean other than Patton set up this prison camp in Heilbronn and we had a half a million prisoners in there

ctx.x: Did you notice, was there a resentment from the German population towards Americans, or didn’t you have to deal with that?

We didn’t deal too much with the population. I mean other than Patton set up this prison camp in Heilbronn and we had a half a million prisoners in there, not all Germans, some Hungarians and what have you. And periodically we had to go in there and find the SS men that were amongst them that had been captured, because I mean nobody would talk, nobody would say anything if there was an SS man around. So they picked some of the bigger guys and three or four of us would go in there unarmed and find the SS men, and…
Oh yeah. And this was like a temporary holding place for these soldiers until eventually—
